Why should human beings not likewise take the risk that their new world may slip from their grasp? The new New World is therefore already among us. It is in our hands. It is under construction. It does not have a bounded piece of earth in which a sacred place can be located.
Its interest in land is an interest in deposits of raw materials. It cares only about exploitation, not cultivation.

Where does this New World stand? It removes the ground from under the feet of its previous owners. It treats the surface of the earth the way a sailor treats the sea, not the way a man walking on land treats the earth.

Is there a dialectic in the sequence of the elements? That depends on how far we can grasp the concept of an element historically and set it into motion.
If we can, then the sequence is indeed: land, water, air, fire.
Historical development then moves through this cycle.
Our historical dialectic must begin with these elements, not, as in Hegel’s lectures, with the written material of historical knowledge. Nor should it begin with economic materialism.

Economic materialism possesses only the time-bound truth of the nineteenth century’s self-destruction and is itself an ideological superstructure built over the Industrial Revolution of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

What use is a clear and compelling argument in international law in Germany’s favor today? It always runs into the consequences of the discriminatory concept of war. That concept gives Germany’s opponents the clear conscience they need to strip the defeated party of its rights.
As every day shows anew, it makes a peace treaty internally impossible.
What remains are only measures of punishment, compensation, and reeducation.

Every effort to “normalize” relations with Germany—especially relations between the occupying powers and German state authority—runs into this basic source of all the impossibilities of international law.
A discriminatory concept of war does not permit the normalization of the party that has been discriminated against.
What, then, is a German supposed to do? The following possibilities exist:
Attack the idea of the just war head-on. Openly demonstrate its historical, legal, and moral perversity; show that it is an instrument of civil war, and so on. Hopeless?

Patiently hollow it out from within by positivist means. Normalize things quietly and unofficially. Sabotage the system by cooperating in the development of the legal foundations of the Nuremberg judgments. Deliberately and systematically play the worm in the rotten wood. Use Portia’s method: take them exactly at their word.
Combine these two possibilities, with different people playing different roles.
